U1-D4.text: Identify warning signs of misleading health information.
Evaluate the credibility of a source.
Justify whether a health claim should or should not be trusted.

U5-D1.text: Define probability, house edge, and gambler's fallacy accurately.
Solve a simple probability or expected-value problem correctly.
Explain, in your own words, why house advantage guarantees that gambling businesses profit over time.

U5-D2.text: Match key terms (dopamine/reward pathway, variable reinforcement, near miss, tolerance, chasing losses) to accurate definitions or scenarios.
Describe the mismatch between reward-system and prefrontal-cortex development in the teen brain.
Explain why that mismatch increases adolescent vulnerability to gambling and other addictive behaviors.
Identify risk factors that raise a person's vulnerability to problem gambling.
U5-D2.note: Original said 'name one PERSONAL risk factor in a written reflection'. Tickets never ask for personal disclosure, so this is stated generally; the reflection itself stays a classroom activity.

U5-D3.text: Identify at least three persuasive marketing techniques used in sports-betting advertising.
Identify the intended audience of a betting advertisement.
Explain how these techniques normalize gambling for young people.
Draft a PSA message that addresses at least one of these techniques.

U5-D4.text: Identify warning signs of problem gambling.
Apply every step of a decision-making model to a risk scenario.

U5-D4.note: Performed/observed in class; the ticket tests the knowledge behind it.

U5-D4.text: Identify where to find help for problem gambling (school counselor, trusted adult, helpline).
Describe common financial and social consequences of problem gambling.

U6-D1.text: Summarize the main finding of a credible data source on teen injury risk.
Explain why protective behaviors (seatbelts, helmets) reduce the risk of serious injury.

U6-D2.text: State the first two steps of the Chain of Survival (recognize the emergency, call 911).
Demonstrate correct hand placement for hands-only CPR compressions.
U6-D2.note: Performed/observed in class; the ticket tests the knowledge behind it.

U6-D2.text: Demonstrate a steady, correct compression rate.
U6-D2.note: Performed/observed in class; the ticket tests the knowledge behind it.

U6-D3.text: Correctly sequence the steps of AED use.
Explain how an AED and hands-only CPR work together in the Chain of Survival.
State the fact that corrects a common organ-donation myth.

U6-D5.text: Explain how distraction slows reaction time and raises crash risk.
Identify technology habits that support safety (e.g., no phone near traffic, notification boundaries, careful location sharing).
Distinguish specific, realistic safety commitments from vague ones.
U6-D5.note: Original: 'write one personal safety commitment'. Written commitment stays in class; the ticket tests what makes a commitment specific and realistic.

U7-D1.text: Name the three macronutrients and one general role of each.
Identify a balanced meal using the MyPlate model (proportions from at least four of the five food groups).
Describe the general role of micronutrients (vitamins and minerals).

U7-D2.text: Identify serving size, calories, and key nutrients on a nutrition facts label.
Compare two labeled products using label information.
Explain the difference between serving size and portion size.
Estimate a reasonable portion size using simple visual references.

U7-D3.text: Define the four FITT components (Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type).
Apply FITT to plan a sample physical activity.
Describe how the talk test or a perceived-effort scale shows exercise intensity.

U7-D4.text: Identify the persuasive marketing technique used in a food-packaging or fitness social-media example.
Explain why a health claim should be checked against a credible source.

U7-D5.text: Identify which of the five SMART components a goal includes or is missing.
Recognize a habit-based nutrition or physical-activity goal.
Identify a realistic barrier to reaching a goal.
Match a barrier with a corresponding strategy.

U8-D1.text: Identify accurate facts about puberty (myth vs. fact).
Describe the general physical changes of puberty.
Name a credible source of reproductive health information.

U8-D2.text: Sort relationship characteristics as healthy or unhealthy.
Explain what consent and healthy boundaries mean.
Recognize a clear, respectful way to state a boundary.
U8-D2.note: Original: 'state a personal boundary during role-play'. Practiced in class; ticket uses fictional scenarios only.

U8-D3.text: Describe how STIs and HIV are and are not transmitted.
Identify at least two prevention methods.
Distinguish HIV myths from facts and correct a myth with an accurate fact.

U8-D4.text: Explain why abstinence is presented as the most effective prevention method for pregnancy and STIs.
U8-D4.note: Original criterion said abstinence 'eliminates risk'; objective says 'most effective'. Using the objective's wording (HIV can also spread non-sexually). Please confirm.

U8-D4.text: Apply every step of a decision-making model to a values-based scenario.
Use a clear, respectful refusal statement.
U8-D4.note: Performed/observed in class; the ticket tests the knowledge behind it.

U8-D5.text: Name at least two credible resources appropriate to a given scenario.
Identify where to access reliable help and testing, including confidentiality in general terms.
Identify the features of an accurate, non-judgmental advocacy message.
